# NSPanel HAUI 0.4.5

This release adds a live preview of the panel to the editor, draws every panel
card from the hub's own render, moves firmware updates into the integration, and
brings Day/Night profiles, editable popups, a configurable inside-temperature
sensor and several notification fixes.

## Highlights

- **Live preview in the editor** — the new **Live preview** button
  (`mdi:television-play`) opens an interactive virtual panel for the selected
  device, rendered from the real hub code: tap, drag and swipe with mouse or
  finger, press the hardware buttons, trigger the idle timeout. **Sandbox mode**
  (the default) simulates every entity change; **Live mode** calls Home
  Assistant, including the panel's relays from the hardware buttons, except for
  the panel's settings. A **Show entities** switch names the entity under the
  mouse, and **Reset sandbox** restores the simulated entities without leaving
  sandbox mode. The preview fires no events for automations and never installs
  updates. Contributed by
  [@jameshiscott](https://github.com/jameshiscott) in
  [#85](https://github.com/happydasch/nspanel_haui/pull/85) and
  [#86](https://github.com/happydasch/nspanel_haui/pull/86).
- **Panel cards drawn by the hub** — every panel card (user panels, system
  panels, popup aliases, landscape and portrait) shows its panel exactly as the
  device does: the hub renders the panel and the card replays the hub's display
  output in the Nextion simulator, built from the real HMI layout. Entity
  values, translations in the device's language, templates, the clock, the
  weather forecast and colour overrides are the hub's own; unsaved edits show
  right away. The dozens of per-type preview renderers are gone.
- **Every popup can be edited** — the editor's System Panels section offers
  **Edit** on every popup (`popup_*`), not only six entity popups. An edited
  popup keeps the built-in defaults it does not set, keeps its key and never
  joins navigation. On the popups the hub drives (Notify, Select, Unlock) the
  editor hides **Panel pin** and **Close automatically after** and the hub
  ignores them. System, Blank, Settings and About stay fixed.
- **Long press to go back** — Clock, ClockTwo and Weather panels have no header
  buttons and could only be left by swiping. The new **Long press to go back**
  panel option (Advanced section) goes back on a one-second hold anywhere: to
  the panel this one was opened from, or to the home panel. Also contributed by
  [@jameshiscott](https://github.com/jameshiscott).
- **Firmware updates moved to the integration** — the **HAUI Firmware** update
  entity now lives in the integration, reads the release manifest itself and
  installs through the firmware's `install_firmware_url` action. A new
  **Firmware update channel** setting (`stable` or `dev`) and an optional
  **Firmware manifest URL** control which manifest it follows.
- **Day/Night Profiles** — each device can select Day and Night display settings
  by a fixed local window or Home Assistant sunrise/sunset with minute offsets.
  Profiles cover brightness, dimming, page/idle target and display-off behavior;
  the independent Sleep schedule keeps its existing precedence.
- **Inside temperature sensor picker** — clock and weather panels can use any
  `sensor` entity for the inside temperature; leave empty for the NSPanel's
  internal sensor.
- **Notification fixes and options** — optional `timeout` auto-dismiss,
  multi-line text renders its line breaks, icon-less notifications use the full
  text width (no severity default icon), long messages are wrapped with the
  display fonts' real glyph widths, paging keeps the **Dismiss** button, and
  the alarm panel gains action button options (hidden arm modes, action icons,
  text/background colours).

## Before updating

- **The display TFT follows the firmware manifest.** The editor's TFT picker
  lists only the manifest's TFT (plus **From URL**); installing an older
  release's TFT by version is no longer possible.
- **Panels on firmware 0.4.2 or earlier must be updated once by hand** (ESPHome
  or **Install firmware → From URL**), because their firmware lacks the
  `install_firmware_url` action.
- **Custom firmware builds fail closed.** A custom build reports its variant and
  is never offered or installed the public universal release image; flash the
  new release once by hand, then the hub can update it again.
- A test panel that followed local test releases through the firmware
  `firmware_manifest_url` substitution needs the new **Firmware manifest URL**
  device setting instead.
- **Native OTA is encrypted with the API key** instead of an OTA password
  ([#81](https://github.com/happydasch/nspanel_haui/issues/81)). Panels on 0.4
  firmware need nothing; older firmware needs one wireless install with a
  migration block, and a `password:` on the OTA block of your own YAML must be
  removed. See
  [ESPHome → Encrypted native OTA](docs/esphome.md#encrypted-native-ota).

See [Upgrading → Firmware updates](docs/upgrading.md#11-firmware-updates-moved-to-the-integration)
for the full migration steps.

## Known limits

- The live preview and panel cards render fonts with Home Assistant's Roboto
  sized to the Nextion's, so text can sit a pixel or two differently from the
  panel.
- A device has one virtual app shared by its open previews and its panel cards,
  so Sandbox/Live mode belongs to the device. Switching it in one browser tab
  changes it for every open preview of that device; other tabs' toggles may
  keep showing their old mode until reopened.
